prompt: Hypothetical. A trader plans to hold 10 shares overnight, but the order screen shows MIS because she picked it by mistake. What is the most likely consequence?

options.text: Nothing changes. MIS and CNC are the same product.
The position is meant to close within the same session, and the broker's auto square-off rules may close it.
The shares go into her demat account the same afternoon.
The product type only changes the name shown on the screen.

explanations.a: MIS and CNC are different products. MIS is meant to close within the same session.
explanations.c: This describes a delivery holding under CNC. It does not describe a same-day MIS position.
explanations.d: The product type changes how long the trade is meant to last and how it is handled by the broker.

prompt: Hypothetical. You buy 10 shares at Rs 250. What is the order value before charges, in rupees?
Hypothetical. The order value is Rs 2,500. The price moves 1% against you. What is the loss in rupees, before charges?
solution: 1% of Rs 2,500 = 2,500 x 0.01 = Rs 25. Check: 10% of Rs 2,500 is Rs 250, and one tenth of that is Rs 25.

prompt: A trader writes: 'MIS is cheaper, so I will use it for my three-week plan.' Which part of this reasoning is wrong?

options.text: MIS is cheaper, so it is the right product for my plan.
The product should follow the holding period.
Whether MIS is cheaper for me is a fact to check in the cost preview.

explanations.a: This is correct. The plan does last three weeks, and that is the fact the product choice must follow.
explanations.c: This is correct. The holding period decides the product, not the cost.
explanations.d: This is correct. Cost is a fact to check in the preview, but it is not the reason to pick a product.

prompt: Why does this book keep beginners with CNC?

options.text: CNC has no risk, so beginners are safe with it.
The book's method holds trades for days or weeks, and that style uses CNC. Intraday trading is a higher-risk style.
CNC lets you sell at any time, whatever the settlement status.
MIS has no risk because it closes the same day.

explanations.a: CNC still carries market risk. A holding for weeks can fall in price.
explanations.c: Holdings still follow settlement timing. See the chapter on demat accounts and settlement.
explanations.d: MIS carries risk. It uses margin, which is leverage, and a same-day position can still lose money quickly.

prompt: What does the product type mainly tell the broker?

options.text: How long the trade is meant to last and how it is settled.
The stop price for the trade.
The profit target for the trade.

explanations.a: The stock is chosen by your plan and the symbol you pick. The product type does not choose the stock.
explanations.c: The stop price is set in the order itself, not by the product type.
explanations.d: A profit target is part of your plan. The product type does not set it.
